messages:
Maya (Sales): Hey everyone — ACME legal sent over the contract but they raised two blockers: security questionnaire answers and POC perf. Their engineering lead reports TTFT spikes during burst tests (800-1.2s). Can we swarm and give a short troubleshooting runbook + short answers for the questionnaire?
Alice (ACME): Confirming. Our load: 20 concurrent users hitting the model with chat-like prompts (avg input ~120 tokens, expected response ~60 tokens). Region: us-west-2. We also saw occasional 429s and a few 'kv_cache miss' logs.
Liam (SE): Thanks @Maya @Alice. First ask: which model variant are you using? Also paste a sample request id from the logs (request_id). 429s usually mean per-second concurrency throttle or burst cap.
Alice (ACME): Sample request_id: req_20260301_71b9. Model is rwinf-redwood-13b-v1, default config from the dashboard.
Priya (Eng-Oncall): Looking at that request id in our logs — I can see increased queue latency around the time of the spike. Two things to check immediately:
- batching config: dashboard shows min_batch_timeout_ms=5 and max_batch_size=64 which can hurt TTFT for small prompt sizes. Recommend setting min_batch_timeout_ms=2 and max_batch_size=16 for chat workloads.
- cache warmup: KV cache miss ratio is ~0.78 for that session. Enable prefix caching and run a short warmup to populate KV cache.
Liam (SE): Repro commands for ACME to run a quick diagnostic (paste into their env):
```bash
# single request for timing (prints ttft_ms)
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"rwinf-redwood-13b-v1","input":"<replace-with-sample>","stream":false}' \
  https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate | jq '.timing.first_token_ms'
```
And to collect a short latency distribution over 30 requests: run a bash loop and report p50/p95/p99.
Alice (ACME): Running the single request now — getting ~920ms first_token_ms.
Priya (Eng-Oncall): Ok that's in line with their spike. Next try this overlay to the POC config to force smaller batches and enable prefix cache:
```yaml
batching:
  max_batch_size: 16
  min_batch_timeout_ms: 2
cache:
  prefix_cache: true
  warmup_tokens: 256
routing_policy:
  prefer_low_latency: true
```
Apply via the Console -> POCs -> "overrides" (you can paste as a YAML). This should bring down median TTFT for small prompts.
Liam (SE): Also confirm whether ACME is using streaming. If streaming=true we sometimes see higher first-token if the client waits for the initial setup; try stream=false for raw TTFT measurement.
Alice (ACME): We're using streaming=true in prod. For diagnostics I switched to stream=false and saw 780ms.
Jorge (Security): For the questionnaire: data residency + KMS answers ready. Short answers for legal: we support dedicated VPC, customer-managed KMS/HSM for Private, and logs can be routed to a customer SIEM via S3->CloudTrail. I'll drop the canned answers in the thread in a minute.
Ethan (AE): Pricing note for contract: POC customers get 90 days of trial credits in this deal. If we recommend Dedicated for predictable latency, estimate uplift ~2.5x on base hosted per-token to cover reserved GPU pool (ballpark — I'll get a firm number by EOD).
deploy-bot: Canary deployment rwinf-redwood-13b-v1 -> canary-2026-03-01 triggered by Liam
Priya (Eng-Oncall): Quick log snippet for the period (redacted):
"[2026-03-01T15:12:03Z] req=req_20260301_71b9 queue_ms=320 exec_ms=420 kv_cache_miss=true batch_size=48"
That queue_ms is the main contributor to TTFT here. Reducing batch size should cut queue_ms substantially.
Liam (SE): If the customer still needs throughput after reducing batch size we can: (1) add a small autoscale policy to add an extra worker during spikes, or (2) enable model quantized variant (rwinf-redwood-13b-4bit) which reduces exec_ms. Both have cost tradeoffs.
Alice (ACME): If we enable the quantized variant, any functional delta we need to worry about for our prompts? We care about answer quality for financial content.
Liam (SE): For finance prompts we'd prefer to run a quick quality eval on a small prompt set. Quantized 4-bit typically has negligible difference on many tasks but let's run 20 evals. I can spin that up.
Maya (Sales): Action list: @Liam run 20 evals on customer's sample prompts against quantized variant (owner: Liam) — due EOD. @Priya apply the batching/cache overlay to the customer's POC config and rerun the 30-request timing (owner: Priya) — update within 2 hours. @Jorge post canned security answers in this thread (owner: Jorge). @Ethan confirm pricing uplift number (owner: Ethan). @Alice please attach a few representative prompt examples and the exported p50/p95 after overlay.
Alice (ACME): Will attach prompts and results in ~30m. Thanks for the quick triage.
Priya (Eng-Oncall): Applying overlay now. I'll ping when we have the new numbers.
Liam (SE): Starting the eval run now.
Jorge (Security): Canned Q&A posted: "We support VPC/Private deploys, customer-managed KMS, SOC2 Type II, and can restrict telemetry — see attached boilerplate." (I'll DM legal for any edits.)
Priya (Eng-Oncall): Update: after overlay and a short warmup run of 200 tokens x 10 requests, new timings: p50=210ms p95=380ms p99=610ms for non-streaming requests in us-west-2. Streaming first-byte was ~270ms. No 429s observed during the test window.
Alice (ACME): That's a big improvement. I'll re-run our load test and share p50/p95/p99 shortly.
Maya (Sales): Great. I'll consolidate answers for legal and loop in account team. Thanks team — great swarm.
Ethan (AE): I'll follow up on pricing and share a short note with committed options vs burst capacity by EOD.
Liam (SE): If anything regresses please @priaya and tag this thread. We'll keep the overlay live in the POC until we finalize capacity decisions.
(END)
